findings.reason: without a stated size decision the implementing node must pick, and whichever it picks the done-when either fails on sizes or on "no script keeps a figure-export function of its own".
findings.text: §2 now requires that "the scripts still write every file they write today, in the same formats and at the same sizes", but four tracked `docs/figures/discovery-to-mapping/*.svg` and `docs/figures/jt60sa-mapping-study/agreement.svg` declare `width="1008pt"` (35.6 cm) today and are written by plain `fig.savefig` with no size rewrite, while §1 fixes the shared export to declare the slide width (`save_figure` writes `width="31.1cm"` and a height derived from it); routing those five figures through the shared function necessarily changes their declared size, so the section cannot be satisfied as written and a worker must either republish them at a new size or leave them on a script-local export — each violating one clause, and the author has not said which.

response_events.note: Section 2 at version 3 decides it: every vector figure takes the physical size the shared function derives, figures that declared another size are listed before and after, and the invariant is the aspect ratio, not the declared size.
